..
Issued at 257 AM EDT Sat Aug 8 2026

Today-Tonight...Inverted trough will continue to shift west-
northwest of the area, with Atlantic ridge axis remaining north of 
the area. Low level south-southeast flow may still transport showers 
and isolated storms onshore along the coast, especially south of the 
Cape this morning. Some isolated showers may also continue near to 
NW of I-4 through daybreak. A moist airmass will remain in the wake 
of the trough today, with PW values still ranging from 2.0-2.3" for 
much of the area. This will continue higher rain chances today (up 
to 40-70%), with scattered to numerous showers and storms developing 
through the afternoon and evening as sea breeze boundaries push 
inland. Greatest coverage of this activity will be focused near to 
west of I-95 through the I-4 corridor region. 

The moist airmass in place and slower storm motion due to weaker 
southerly steering winds, will continue the threat for locally heavy 
to excessive rainfall today. Persistent heavier showers and storms 
will be capable of producing quick rainfall totals of 2-4", with 
isolated spots to around 5" possible, leading to localized flooding 
issues. The area remains outlooked in a Marginal Risk (1/4) of 
excessive rainfall today. Some drier air aloft will also begin to 
work its way into the region, with DCAPE values rising to 800-1000 
J/kg. This will continue the threat for strong wind gusts of 40-50 
mph and frequent lightning from any stronger storms. Convection will 
gradually wind down through the evening across the interior, with 
mostly dry conditions overnight. 

A little less cloud cover to start today should allow highs to reach 
more normal values this afternoon, in the low 90s for most 
locations. These seasonably hot temperatures combined with the humid 
conditions from the moist airmass in place, will lead to a rise in 
heat index values today, peaking around 102-107F this afternoon 
ahead of developing showers and storms. Practicing heat safety will 
be important with these conditions. Stay hydrated, take plenty of 
breaks in the A/C and never leave children or pets unattended in a 
vehicle. Also, if trying to beat the heat by heading to the beach, 
be aware a High Risk of rip currents continues along the east 
central Florida coast due to lingering swells. 

Sunday...Atlantic ridge axis will begin a southward shift tomorrow, 
but will largely remain north of the area, with onshore winds out of 
the east-southeast forecast. Aloft, a mid-level ridge will begin to 
nudge its way in from the east and combine with the advection of 
drier air aloft (PW values falling to 1.8-2.0") to lead to a 
decrease in showers and storms tomorrow. However, still expecting 
scattered coverage of this activity (PoPs 30-50%) into the 
afternoon/evening, especially across the interior. Storm threats of 
frequent lightning, strong wind gusts and locally heavy rainfall 
will continue with any stronger convection. Hot and humid conditions 
persist, with highs in the low 90s, and potentially reaching the 
mid 90s northwest of I-4. Peak heat index values still forecast 
around 102-107F in the afternoon. 

Monday-Friday...Ridge aloft continues to build west and across 
Florida, remaining in place across the region through all of next 
week. This will lead to continued hot and humid conditions and also 
combine with drier air moving in aloft to produce below normal storm 
coverage each day. Afternoon/evening shower and storm chances drop 
to 20-30% Monday and Tuesday and 20% or less Wednesday-Friday. 
Atlantic ridge axis shifting southward and eventually south of 
central FL into mid/late week will also eventually switch prevailing 
flow offshore, which will put an end to any potential for isolated 
onshore moving showers during the overnight/early morning hours. 
With limited breaks from afternoon convection, heat impacts will 
rise into next week, with highs near to above normal in the low to 
mid 90s leading to a widespread Moderate to Major HeatRisk. Peak
heat index values will continue to solidly reach 102-107F, but 
for portions of the area could see these values nudge toward Heat
Advisory criteria of 108-110F, especially Tuesday onward. Will
continue to monitor the need for any Heat Advisories as we head
into next week.
